cond_0001.intro: We are looking for a Research Scientist 2 to join our team.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Under general supervision of a Research Scientist 4, provides support to the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry's Ambient Air Laboratory. Specific duties include:
Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)
Prepare passive sampling devices for field sampling, including SUMMA canisters and flow controllers specific to EPA air methods. Prepare calibration and quality control standards, and research and analyze these standards and field samples using Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry instrumentation following USEPA TO-15 methodology. Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Research and review analytical data and generate analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Research and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Maintain competency and compliance with methods by researching and performing annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Research and troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)
Provide support by assisting with the research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds using EPA methodologies, as needed. Assist in data review for these methods.
Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Supervise staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.
Assist with general laboratory management and mission (10%)
Assist with training staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Manage budgetary needs and procure supplies. Maintain clean and safe work environment. Interact with instrument and consumable supply vendors to troubleshoot issues, procure appropriate supplies, and keep current with new techniques and supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in the natural sciences and three years of post-degree professional research experience in an appropriate field, or a Master's degree in the appropriate field and two years of such experience; or a doctorate in the appropriate field.
Experience working independently in a laboratory setting.
Minimum 1-3 years of supervisory experience.
Familiarity with EPA methodologies relevant to drinking water and/or air analysis.
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with Microsoft Excel as it applies to quality control and data review.
Experience with analytical instrumentation such as Gas Chromatography or Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry.

Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)
Prepare passive sampling devices for field sampling, including SUMMA canisters and flow controllers specific to EPA air methods. Prepare calibration and quality control standards, and research and analyze these standards and field samples using Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry instrumentation following USEPA TO-15 methodology. Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Research and review analytical data and generate analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Research and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Maintain competency and compliance with methods by researching and performing annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Research and troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)
Provide support by assisting with the research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds using EPA methodologies, as needed. Assist in data review for these methods.
Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Supervise staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.
Assist with general laboratory management and mission (10%)
Assist with training staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Manage budgetary needs and procure supplies. Maintain clean and safe work environment. Interact with instrument and consumable supply vendors to troubleshoot issues, procure appropriate supplies, and keep current with new techniques and supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.
cond_0010.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in the natural sciences and three years of post-degree professional research experience in an appropriate field, or a Master's degree in the appropriate field and two years of such experience; or a doctorate in the appropriate field. Experience working independently in a laboratory setting, familiarity with Microsoft Excel as it applies to quality control and data review, minimum 1-3 years of supervisory experience, familiarity with EPA methodologies relevant to drinking water and/or air analysis, and experience with analytical instrumentation such as Gas Chromatography or Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry.
Dependent upon the initial assignment or subsequent reassignment of this position satisfactory background checks may be required. Additionally, exposure to potentially hazardous substances may be involved with this position; the selected candidate may be required to wear personal protective clothing and equipment, and may undergo pre-employment and/or periodic health evaluations and receive specific immunizations.

cond_0075.intro: We are looking for a Research Scientist 2 to join our team.
cond_0075.responsibilities:
Under general supervision of a Research Scientist 4, provides support to the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry's Ambient Air Laboratory. Specific duties include:
Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)
Prepare passive sampling devices for field sampling, including SUMMA canisters and flow controllers specific to EPA air methods. Prepare calibration and quality control standards, and research and analyze these standards and field samples using Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry instrumentation following USEPA TO-15 methodology. Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Research and review analytical data and generate analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Research and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Maintain competency and compliance with methods by researching and performing annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Research and troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)
Provide support by assisting with the research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds using EPA methodologies, as needed. Assist in data review for these methods.
Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Supervise staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.
Assist with general laboratory management and mission (10%)
Assist with training staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Manage budgetary needs and procure supplies. Maintain clean and safe work environment. Interact with instrument and consumable supply vendors to troubleshoot issues, procure appropriate supplies, and keep current with new techniques and supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.
Dependent upon the initial assignment or subsequent reassignment of this position satisfactory background checks may be required. Additionally, exposure to potentially hazardous substances may be involved with this position; the selected candidate may be required to wear personal protective clothing and equipment, and may undergo pre-employment and/or periodic health evaluations and receive specific immunizations.
cond_0075.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in the natural sciences and around three years of post-degree professional research experience in an appropriate field, or a Master's degree in the appropriate field and around two years of such experience, or a doctorate in the appropriate field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience working independently in a laboratory setting.
Around 1–3 years of supervisory experience.
Working knowledge of EPA methodologies relevant to drinking water and/or air analysis.
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with Microsoft Excel as it applies to quality control and data review.
Experience with analytical instrumentation such as Gas Chromatography or Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry.

Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)

Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Research and review analytical data and generate analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Research and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Maintain competency and compliance with methods by researching and performing annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Research and troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)

Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Supervise staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.

Assist with training staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Manage budgetary needs and procure supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.

Dependent upon the initial assignment or subsequent reassignment of this position satisfactory background checks may be required. cond_0125.intro: Under general supervision of a Research Scientist 4, this role leads work in the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry's Ambient Air Laboratory.
cond_0125.responsibilities:
Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)
Prepare passive sampling devices for field sampling, including SUMMA canisters and flow controllers specific to EPA air methods. Execute preparation of calibration and quality control standards, and analyze these standards and field samples using Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry instrumentation following USEPA TO-15 methodology. Own and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Review analytical data and generate analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Maintain competency and compliance with methods by performing annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)
Lead analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds using EPA methodologies, as needed. Drive data review for these methods.
Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Direct staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.
Assist with general laboratory management and mission (10%)
Train staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Manage budgetary needs and procure supplies. Maintain clean and safe work environment. Interact with instrument and consumable supply vendors to troubleshoot issues, procure appropriate supplies, and keep current with new techniques and supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.
cond_0125.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in the natural sciences and three years of post-degree professional research experience in an appropriate field, or a Master's degree in the appropriate field and two years of such experience; or a doctorate in the appropriate field. Experience working independently in a laboratory setting, familiarity with Microsoft Excel as it applies to quality control and data review, minimum 1-3 years of supervisory experience, familiarity with EPA methodologies relevant to drinking water and/or air analysis, and experience with analytical instrumentation such as Gas Chromatography or Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry.
Dependent upon the initial assignment or subsequent reassignment of this position satisfactory background checks may be required. Additionally, exposure to potentially hazardous substances may be involved with this position; the selected candidate may be required to wear personal protective clothing and equipment, and may undergo pre-employment and/or periodic health evaluations and receive specific immunizations.

cond_0145.intro: We are looking for a Research Scientist 2 to join our team.
cond_0145.responsibilities:
Under general supervision of a Research Scientist 4, provides support to the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry's Ambient Air Laboratory. Specific duties include:
Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)
Prepare passive sampling devices for field sampling, including SUMMA canisters and flow controllers specific to EPA air methods. Prepare calibration and quality control standards, and research and analyze these standards and field samples using Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry instrumentation following USEPA TO-15 methodology. Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Research and review analytical data and generate analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Research and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Maintain competency and compliance with methods by researching and performing annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Research and troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)
Provide support by assisting with the research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds using EPA methodologies, as needed. Assist in data review for these methods.
Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Supervise staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.
Assist with general laboratory management and mission (10%)
Assist with training staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Manage budgetary needs and procure supplies. Maintain clean and safe work environment. Interact with instrument and consumable supply vendors to troubleshoot issues, procure appropriate supplies, and keep current with new techniques and supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.
cond_0145.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in the natural sciences and three years of post-degree professional research experience in an appropriate field, or a Master's degree in the appropriate field and two years of such experience; or a doctorate in the appropriate field.
Experience working independently in a laboratory setting.
Minimum 1-3 years of supervisory experience.
Familiarity with EPA methodologies relevant to drinking water and/or air analysis.
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with Microsoft Excel as it applies to quality control and data review.
Experience with analytical instrumentation such as Gas Chromatography or Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry.

cond_0311.intro: Under general supervision of a Research Scientist 4, this role provides support to the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry's Ambient Air Laboratory at [Company name masked] in [Location masked]. Most people become stronger in this kind of analytical and laboratory work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
cond_0311.responsibilities:
Specific duties include:
Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)
Prepare passive sampling devices for field sampling, including SUMMA canisters and flow controllers specific to EPA air methods. Prepare calibration and quality control standards, and research and analyze these standards and field samples using Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry instrumentation following USEPA TO-15 methodology. Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Research and review analytical data and generate analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Research and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Maintain competency and compliance with methods by researching and performing annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Research and troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)
Provide support by assisting with the research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds using EPA methodologies, as needed. Assist in data review for these methods.
Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Supervise staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.
Assist with general laboratory management and mission (10%)
Assist with training staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Manage budgetary needs and procure supplies. Maintain clean and safe work environment. Interact with instrument and consumable supply vendors to troubleshoot issues, procure appropriate supplies, and keep current with new techniques and supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.
Additional Comments:
Dependent upon the initial assignment or subsequent reassignment of this position satisfactory background checks may be required. Additionally, exposure to potentially hazardous substances may be involved with this position; the selected candidate may be required to wear personal protective clothing and equipment, and may undergo pre-employment and/or periodic health evaluations and receive specific immunizations.
cond_0311.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in the natural sciences and three years of post-degree professional research experience in an appropriate field, or a Master's degree in the appropriate field and two years of such experience; or a doctorate in the appropriate field.
Experience working independently in a laboratory setting.
Minimum 1-3 years of supervisory experience.
Familiarity with EPA methodologies relevant to drinking water and/or air analysis.
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with Microsoft Excel as it applies to quality control and data review.
Experience with analytical instrumentation such as Gas Chromatography or Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry.

cond_0332.intro: Under general supervision of a Research Scientist 4, this role provides support to the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry's Ambient Air Laboratory.
cond_0332.responsibilities:
Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)
Prepare passive sampling devices for field sampling, including SUMMA canisters and flow controllers specific to EPA air methods. Prepare calibration and quality control standards, and execute research and analysis of these standards and field samples using Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry instrumentation following USEPA TO-15 methodology. Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Review analytical data and generate analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Maintain competency and compliance with methods by performing annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)
Lead analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds using EPA methodologies, as needed. Own data review for these methods.
Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Directly supervise staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.
General laboratory management and mission (10%)
Train staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Manage budgetary needs and procure supplies. Maintain a clean and safe work environment. Lead coordination with instrument and consumable supply vendors to troubleshoot issues, procure appropriate supplies, and keep current with new techniques and supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.

cond_0371.intro: We are looking for a Research Scientist 2 to join our team.
cond_0371.responsibilities:
Under general supervision of a Research Scientist 4, provides support to the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry's Ambient Air Laboratory. Specific duties include:
Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)
Prepare passive sampling devices for field sampling, including SUMMA canisters and flow controllers specific to EPA air methods. Prepare calibration and quality control standards, and research and analyze these standards and field samples using Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry instrumentation following USEPA TO-15 methodology. Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Research and review analytical data and generate analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Research and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Maintain competency and compliance with methods by researching and performing annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Research and troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)
Provide support by assisting with the research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds using EPA methodologies, as needed. Assist in data review for these methods.
Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Supervise staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.
Assist with general laboratory management and mission (10%)
Assist with training staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Manage budgetary needs and procure supplies. Maintain clean and safe work environment. Interact with instrument and consumable supply vendors to troubleshoot issues, procure appropriate supplies, and keep current with new techniques and supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.
Additional Comments
Dependent upon the initial assignment or subsequent reassignment of this position satisfactory background checks may be required. Additionally, exposure to potentially hazardous substances may be involved with this position; the selected candidate may be required to wear personal protective clothing and equipment, and may undergo pre-employment and/or periodic health evaluations and receive specific immunizations.
cond_0371.requirements: Bachelor's degree in the natural sciences required; advanced degree strongly preferred. Candidates with a Master's degree must have a minimum of two years of demonstrated expertise in an appropriate field; those with a doctorate are considered to have met the experience threshold. Candidates holding only a Bachelor's degree must have a minimum of three years of demonstrated post-degree professional research experience in an appropriate field. Proven track record of working independently in a laboratory setting. Deep knowledge of Microsoft Excel as it applies to quality control and data review. Minimum 3 years of supervisory experience. Advanced knowledge of EPA methodologies relevant to drinking water and/or air analysis. Expertise in analytical instrumentation such as Gas Chromatography or Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry.

cond_0453.responsibilities:
Under general supervision of a Research Scientist 4, provides support to the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry's Ambient Air Laboratory. Specific duties include:
Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)
Prepare passive sampling devices for field sampling, including SUMMA canisters and flow controllers specific to EPA air methods. Prepare calibration and quality control standards, and research and analyze these standards and field samples using Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry instrumentation following USEPA TO-15 methodology. Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Research and review analytical data and generate analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Research and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Maintain competency and compliance with methods by researching and performing annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Research and troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)
Provide support by assisting with the research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds using EPA methodologies, as needed. Assist in data review for these methods.
Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Supervise staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.
Assist with general laboratory management and mission (10%)
Assist with training staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Manage budgetary needs and procure supplies. Maintain clean and safe work environment. Interact with instrument and consumable supply vendors to troubleshoot issues, procure appropriate supplies, and keep current with new techniques and supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.
Dependent upon the initial assignment or subsequent reassignment of this position satisfactory background checks may be required. Additionally, exposure to potentially hazardous substances may be involved with this position; the selected candidate may be required to wear personal protective clothing and equipment, and may undergo pre-employment and/or periodic health evaluations and receive specific immunizations.
cond_0453.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in the natural sciences and around three years of post-degree professional research experience in an appropriate field, or a Master's degree in the appropriate field and around two years of such experience, or a doctorate in the appropriate field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience working independently in a laboratory setting.
Around 1–3 years of supervisory experience.
Working knowledge of EPA methodologies relevant to drinking water and/or air analysis.
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with Microsoft Excel as it applies to quality control and data review.
Experience with analytical instrumentation such as Gas Chromatography or Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry.

cond_0522.intro: Under general supervision of a Research Scientist 4, this role supports the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry's Ambient Air Laboratory through coordination with lab staff and contribution to shared analytical and compliance work.
cond_0522.responsibilities:
Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)
Coordinate the preparation of passive sampling devices for field sampling, including SUMMA canisters and flow controllers specific to EPA air methods. Prepare calibration and quality control standards, and work with the team to analyze these standards and field samples using Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry instrumentation following USEPA TO-15 methodology. Help maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Review analytical data together with colleagues and contribute to generating analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Help ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Support the lab's competency and compliance by coordinating and performing annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Work with others to troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)
Assist with the research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds using EPA methodologies, as needed. Assist in data review for these methods.
Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Supervise staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and help ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.
Assist with general laboratory management and mission (10%)
Assist with training staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Help maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Coordinate budgetary needs and procure supplies. Maintain a clean and safe work environment. Work alongside instrument and consumable supply vendors to troubleshoot issues, procure appropriate supplies, and keep current with new techniques and supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.
cond_0522.requirements: Bachelor's degree in the natural sciences and three years of post-degree professional research experience in an appropriate field, or a Master's degree in the appropriate field and two years of such experience; or a doctorate in the appropriate field. Experience working independently in a laboratory setting, familiarity with Microsoft Excel as it applies to quality control and data review, minimum 1-3 years of supervisory experience, familiarity with EPA methodologies relevant to drinking water and/or air analysis, and experience with analytical instrumentation such as Gas Chromatography or Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry.

Under general supervision of a Research Scientist 4, provides support to the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry's Ambient Air Laboratory. Specific duties include:
Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)
Prepare passive sampling devices for field sampling, including SUMMA canisters and flow controllers specific to EPA air methods. Prepare calibration and quality control standards, and research and analyze these standards and field samples using Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry instrumentation following USEPA TO-15 methodology. Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Research and review analytical data and generate analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Research and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Maintain competency and compliance with methods by researching and performing annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Research and troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)
Provide support by assisting with the research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds using EPA methodologies, as needed. Assist in data review for these methods.
Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Supervise staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.
Assist with general laboratory management and mission (10%)
Assist with training staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Manage budgetary needs and procure supplies. Maintain clean and safe work environment. Interact with instrument and consumable supply vendors to troubleshoot issues, procure appropriate supplies, and keep current with new techniques and supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.
Additional Comments
Dependent upon the initial assignment or subsequent reassignment of this position satisfactory background checks may be required. Additionally, exposure to potentially hazardous substances may be involved with this position; the selected candidate may be required to wear personal protective clothing and equipment, and may undergo pre-employment and/or periodic health evaluations and receive specific immunizations.
cond_0533.requirements: Bachelor's degree in the natural sciences required; advanced degree strongly preferred. Candidates with a Master's degree must have a minimum of two years of demonstrated expertise in an appropriate field; those with a doctorate are considered to have met the experience threshold. Candidates holding only a Bachelor's degree must have a minimum of three years of demonstrated post-degree professional research experience in an appropriate field. Proven track record of working independently in a laboratory setting. Deep knowledge of Microsoft Excel as it applies to quality control and data review. Minimum 3 years of supervisory experience. Advanced knowledge of EPA methodologies relevant to drinking water and/or air analysis. Expertise in analytical instrumentation such as Gas Chromatography or Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry.
cond_0533.workplace_support: We believe growth happens in supportive environments, not in isolation. Through mentorship, collaboration, and shared accountability, we create space for employees to learn, contribute, and succeed.

cond_0544.intro: Under general supervision of a Research Scientist 4, this role provides support to the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry's Ambient Air Laboratory. People who do well here tend to get up to speed quickly on analytical chemistry methods and the logic behind air quality data.
cond_0544.responsibilities:
Specific duties include:
Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)
Prepare passive sampling devices for field sampling, including SUMMA canisters and flow controllers specific to EPA air methods. Prepare calibration and quality control standards, and research and analyze these standards and field samples using Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry instrumentation following USEPA TO-15 methodology. Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Research and review analytical data and generate analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Research and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Maintain competency and compliance with methods by researching and performing annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Research and troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)
Provide support by assisting with the research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds using EPA methodologies, as needed. Assist in data review for these methods.
Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Supervise staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.
Assist with general laboratory management and mission (10%)
Assist with training staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Manage budgetary needs and procure supplies. Maintain clean and safe work environment. Interact with instrument and consumable supply vendors to troubleshoot issues, procure appropriate supplies, and keep current with new techniques and supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.
cond_0544.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in the natural sciences and three years of post-degree professional research experience in an appropriate field, or a Master's degree in the appropriate field and two years of such experience, or a doctorate in the appropriate field.
Experience working independently in a laboratory setting.
Minimum 1-3 years of supervisory experience.
Familiarity with EPA methodologies relevant to drinking water and/or air analysis.
Experience with analytical instrumentation such as Gas Chromatography or Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry.
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with Microsoft Excel as it applies to quality control and data review.
Dependent upon the initial assignment or subsequent reassignment of this position satisfactory background checks may be required. Additionally, exposure to potentially hazardous substances may be involved with this position; the selected candidate may be required to wear personal protective clothing and equipment, and may undergo pre-employment and/or periodic health evaluations and receive specific immunizations.

cond_0605.intro: We are looking for a Research Scientist 2 to join our team.
cond_0605.responsibilities:
Under general supervision of a Research Scientist 4, provides support to the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry's Ambient Air Laboratory. Specific duties include:
Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)
Prepare passive sampling devices for field sampling, including SUMMA canisters and flow controllers specific to EPA air methods. Prepare calibration and quality control standards, and research and analyze these standards and field samples using Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry instrumentation following USEPA TO-15 methodology. Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Research and review analytical data and generate analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Research and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Maintain competency and compliance with methods by researching and performing annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Research and troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)
Provide support by assisting with the research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds using EPA methodologies, as needed. Assist in data review for these methods.
Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Supervise staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.
Assist with general laboratory management and mission (10%)
Assist with training staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Manage budgetary needs and procure supplies. Maintain clean and safe work environment. Interact with instrument and consumable supply vendors to troubleshoot issues, procure appropriate supplies, and keep current with new techniques and supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.
Additional Comments
Dependent upon the initial assignment or subsequent reassignment of this position satisfactory background checks may be required. Additionally, exposure to potentially hazardous substances may be involved with this position; the selected candidate may be required to wear personal protective clothing and equipment, and may undergo pre-employment and/or periodic health evaluations and receive specific immunizations.
cond_0605.requirements: Bachelor's degree in the natural sciences required; advanced degree strongly preferred. Candidates with a Master's degree must have a minimum of two years of demonstrated expertise in an appropriate field; those with a doctorate are considered to have met the experience threshold. Candidates holding only a Bachelor's degree must have a minimum of three years of demonstrated post-degree professional research experience in an appropriate field. Proven track record of working independently in a laboratory setting. Deep knowledge of Microsoft Excel as it applies to quality control and data review. Minimum 3 years of supervisory experience. Advanced knowledge of EPA methodologies relevant to drinking water and/or air analysis. Expertise in analytical instrumentation such as Gas Chromatography or Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry.

Bachelor's degree in the natural sciences and three years of post-degree professional research experience in an appropriate field, or a Master's degree in the appropriate field and two years of such experience, or a doctorate in the appropriate field.
Experience working independently in a laboratory setting.
Minimum 1-3 years of supervisory experience.
Familiarity with EPA methodologies relevant to drinking water and/or air analysis.
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with Microsoft Excel as it applies to quality control and data review.
Experience with analytical instrumentation such as Gas Chromatography or Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry.
Dependent upon the initial assignment or subsequent reassignment of this position satisfactory background checks may be required. Additionally, exposure to potentially hazardous substances may be involved with this position; the selected candidate may be required to wear personal protective clothing and equipment, and may undergo pre-employment and/or periodic health evaluations and receive specific immunizations.

cond_0639.intro: Under general supervision of a Research Scientist 4, this role supports the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry's Ambient Air Laboratory, working alongside colleagues to carry out research, analysis, and laboratory operations.
cond_0639.responsibilities:
Research and analysis of ambient air samples. (70%)
Coordinate the preparation of passive sampling devices for field sampling, including SUMMA canisters and flow controllers specific to EPA air methods. Work with the team to prepare calibration and quality control standards, and research and analyze these standards and field samples using Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry instrumentation following USEPA TO-15 methodology. Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures for all work performed under the TO-15 method. Review analytical data together with colleagues and help generate analytical reports for all standards and field samples. Support compliance with pertinent standards and regulations. Maintain equipment calibrations, ensure traceability through proper documentation, and complete required training. Help maintain competency and compliance with methods by coordinating annual Demonstrations of Capability and Method Detection Limit Studies. Maintain instrumentation through preventative maintenance. Work with others to troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (10%)
Assist with the research and analysis of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds using EPA methodologies, as needed. Collaborate on data review for these methods.
Supervise staff within the Laboratory of Organic Analytical Chemistry (10%)
Supervise staff who perform the analysis of volatiles in air using Gas Chromatography/Electron Capture Detector instrumentation following NYSDOH 311-9 methodology. Review and release final data for NYSDOH 311-9 and help ensure compliance with pertinent standards and regulations.
Assist with general laboratory management and mission (10%)
Help train staff for supporting roles within the air laboratory. Maintain adequate supplies for all present and future analyses. Coordinate budgetary needs and procure supplies. Maintain a clean and safe work environment. Work with instrument and consumable supply vendors to troubleshoot issues, procure appropriate supplies, and stay current with new techniques and supplies. Perform other appropriate duties as assigned.
